## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

content.text:
New request (in Spanish): "Yes, and create an online trading system and shiny creatures that none look alike."

So needs:
1. Online trading system (intercambio) — without a backend? We can build an online trade system using peer-to-peer via WebRTC with a signaling? Or via a share code (offline "online-like" trade)? Need actual online? Could use PeerJS/cloud? No API keys. Could implement trade via "Trade Link Codes" using BroadcastChannel/localStorage? That's local only, not online. Could implement P2P via WebRTC manually with a public signaling server? Unreliable. Could use Firebase? No credentials.

Options:
- Use a public WebSocket relay for signaling + WebRTC data channel. There are free public WebSocket echo services, but they don't relay between clients. Could use PubNub? requires keys. Ably? keys. 
- Supabase anonymous? no.
- Use `wss://relay.walletconnect...` no.
- Use `https://ntfy.sh` (public pub/sub) for signaling! Ntfy is a free HTTP pub/sub service; clients can subscribe to topics via SSE and publish messages. Could use for matchmaking signaling, then WebRTC data channel for trade. But CORS for ntfy? It supports CORS. Risk of external availability. Also privacy—topics public.
- Or implement online trade via a simple "Trade Code" that encodes creature data and can be imported/exported (asynchronous link trading). The user asked "sistema online de intercambio" — an online trade network. A share/link code system could be described as online trading via link, but not realtime.
- Better: implement local "Trade Portal" with two modes:
  a) **Link Trade** over WebRTC using a free signaling via ntfy (fallback: copy/paste offer code).
  b) **Trade Codes** offline-friendly: generate offer code, share, import partner code, exchange.

That's complex but doable. However reliability testing online without a partner is hard. Need at least UI and functionality. Could implement a "Trade Link" system where two browser tabs/devices connect via BroadcastChannel (same device) and via WebRTC (online) using manual copy/paste of SDP offer/answer? Manual copy/paste is clunky but works without server: Player A creates offer, shares code; Player B pastes and creates answer; A pastes answer. Both connect via WebRTC then trade. This is genuinely online P2P, no backend. But UX on mobile is rough (copy/paste long SDP codes). Could compress SDP? Use base64 + gzip? Still huge.

Alternative: use `PeerJS` public cloud broker. PeerJS runs a free cloud signaling server `0.peerjs.com` (may still be available). PeerJS CDN? We can vendor peerjs. Create peer with random ID; trade code = peer ID (short). Other player enters code → connects data channel. PeerJS public server might work. This gives a simple online trade: one player hosts, gets 5-letter code, other joins. Data channel exchange. This is the cleanest. Need vendor peerjs (~50KB) and network to 0.peerjs.com at runtime. Can fallback to link codes if connection fails.

We can test both browser contexts connecting through PeerJS cloud. Network available; test.

2. Shiny creatures that "none look alike" — unique shiny variants per individual, not just color swaps. "criaturas brillantes q ninguna se parezca a otra" = shiny creatures where no two look alike. So each shiny should have a unique appearance: procedural pattern/palette variations, sizes, markings. Need implement per-creature visual uniqueness:
- Each creature instance has a `variant` seed / appearance object: seed-based hue shift, accent colors, pattern type (spots, stripes, gradient), body scale, ear/tail accessory, sparkle effect.
- Shiny creatures: unique colors/pattern combos generated from uid, guaranteed unique per individual (maybe palette + pattern + aura + accessory). "Ninguna se parezca a otra" — use seed to generate unique color palette & markings. Also non-shiny same species could have small variations? At least shinies unique.
- Render shiny sparkles/aura in world and battle.
- Creature models need to accept appearance overrides. Currently materials are cached globally by color string, shared. For variants, need per-instance materials for body parts. Could generate unique color palettes and rebuild model with custom materials. `buildCreature(speciesId, appearance)` where appearance = {colors: {...}, seed, pattern, scale, accessory}. But models built with fixed color strings and cached materials. Approach:
  - After building base model, if shiny/appearance, traverse and remap materials based on original color to a unique palette. Material caching means clone materials for variant and adjust color/emissive.
  - Better generate variant by applying color transforms to all materials in the model: build base, then for each unique original color, create a variant color based on seed (HSL rotate/shift), clone material, assign. This yields unique palettes. Add sparkles (Points around creature) and markings maybe.
  - Add pattern overlay: a few emissive spots on body using random positions; attach to model at build time (small spheres) colored by accent. Since model geometry differs, place spots relative to bounding box: compute Box3, add 3-6 small glowing "star freckles" on the sides/front. Works across all species and makes each unique.
  - Accessory: maybe a floating star/crown? Add unique aura color + orbiting orbs count based on seed (1-3). Could add to all shinies; each varies by color/count/pattern.
  - Size variation: scale ±8%.
  - Unique name? Shiny prefix "✦". 
  - Store `appearance: {seed, palette: {...}, aura, size, pattern}` in mon data. For non-shiny, null; for shiny, generated on creation with unique seed ensuring never repeats (uid + random).
  - Ensure "none look alike": palettes from a large color space; combine with aura + star pattern + size. UI shows "Unique shine #<short code>".
- Party/battle display must use appearance. Everywhere buildCreature called with mon (world, battle, thumbnails). Currently world spawn uses species only; battle makeModel uses mon. Need pass mon.appearance.
- Thumbnails: for generic species use base; for shiny we can't regenerate every time? Could generate on demand a thumbnail for the shiny and cache by seed. For party modal, can use CSS sparkle overlay and base art, or generate variant thumbnails. Simpler: create thumbnail via a helper renderer reused? Existing makeThumbnails generates only base. For shiny, we can overlay ✦ badge and use base art; but shiny menu should reflect unique colors. Better generate on demand using a shared offscreen renderer function and cache by appearance seed. Could build during battle catch? We'll implement `renderCreatureThumb(mon)` using a small renderer created after init, with cache; async not needed (sync render). Use same code as makeThumbnails but per mon. GPU contexts: reuse one renderer and remove after; create at startup and keep? Keep a dedicated 256x256 renderer hidden. That's an extra WebGL context but fine (2 total). Actually battle scene + main + thumb renderer = 3 contexts; mobile may limit to 8. Fine.
- Sparkles in world: for shiny wild, add a small Points or 3 orbiting stars around model. Could reuse a `shinyAura` group with 3 tiny octahedrons + point light? Add to wild root in main based on `mon.shiny`/appearance. Battle too: add aura to model groups. Or buildCreature adds aura if appearance provided. Better: buildCreature(species, appearance) adds aura and variant materials, so all contexts get it.

3. Online trading UI:
- Add a "Trade" button in journal/menu (and maybe title).
- Trade modal screen with tabs:
  - Host a Trade: create peer ID, show code (6 chars), wait for partner.
  - Join: enter code, connect.
  - Select a creature from party to offer; see partner's offer; confirm both; execute swap.
- Use PeerJS. Need vendor library. Check npm peerjs.
- Offline fallback: if PeerJS cloud unavailable, let users exchange "Trade Link" codes (base64 JSON of creature) and redeem. But real online requires connection. We can add "Trade Code" mode that generates a code for a creature; receiver imports it (doesn't remove from giver though; could be a "gift"). Hmm. For integrity, P2P.

- Implement a `TradeManager` module:
  - `host()` creates Peer with generated id (prefix + random), waits for connection.
  - `join(code)` connects.
  - Data protocol:
    ```
    {type:'hello', name, party:[...public info], tradeId}
    {type:'offer', mon}
    {type:'ready', offerId}
    {type:'confirm'}
    {type:'complete'}
    {type:'cancel'}
    ```
  - Each side selects a party creature to offer, clicks "Offer"; data sends full mon JSON. Both click "Confirm Trade"; then each removes own offered mon, adds received mon. Need atomic-ish handshake: send final confirmation; when both confirmed, sender executes and sends 'done'; receiver executes.
  - Since no server, if disconnect mid-trade, can duplicate. Handle with confirmation handshake: both must confirm; host orchestrates. Accept risk.
  - Unique shiny remains unique.
  - Trade evolution? Could implement: certain creatures evolve on trade? Not requested. Maybe "trade bond" bonus: received creature gains +1 level or friendship? Nice touch.
  - Show partner online status, connection state, code copy button, QR? Could display code large. Add "Copy code" and "Share" via navigator.share.
  - Mobile-friendly modal.
  - Add PeerJS dependency vendor. Let's check npm peerjs version and file.

- After trade: save, update party HUD, close or stay. Received creature added if party space (they swap same count; remove own then add received). If own offer is last? Party can't be empty? Allow trade but ensure at least one healthy; prevent offering last creature? Enforce party.length>1. Also disallow offering fainted? No, allow but warn; better allow any except last.
- Must use appearance data when serializing.

- PeerJS cloud may require secure context; localhost/https yes.

Let's check network and npm for peerjs.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a 3D Pokémon-style browser game (“Lumen Isles”) for Android with day/night time, rarity-based flute capture, online trading, and unique shiny creatures.

## Requirements
- 3D Pokémon-style game, playable on Android phones/tablets with touch controls.
- Time must change dynamically (day/night cycle).
- Capture must use flutes, with flute types matched to creature level and rarity.
- Rarities must include: mythical, divine, epic, legendary, rare, common, etc.
- Add an online creature trading system.
- Shiny creatures must be unique — no two shinies look alike.
- Shiny spawn rate must vary by rarity.

## Decisions
- Pure static Three.js game, no build step; vendored Three.js locally.
- Original creatures/art/music; no Pokémon assets or trademarks.
- Rarities: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, mythical, divine.
- Six reusable flutes: willow (1), silver (2), amber (3), moonstone (4), aurora (5), celestial (6).
- Required flute tier = rarity tier, +1 for rarity below legendary at level ≥10; cap 6.
- Flutes unlocked by progression: willow start, silver at 2 species caught, amber at 3, moonstone at 5, aurora at 6, celestial after guardian defeat.
- Shiny odds by rarity: common 1/150, uncommon 1/240, rare 1/420, epic 1/750, legendary 1/1600, mythical 1/3000, divine 1/5000.
- Shiny uniqueness via per-creature seed → unique palette, aura orbs, star-freckle constellation, optional ring, sparkle rhythm.
- Online trade planned with PeerJS public cloud (`0.peerjs.com` returned HTTP 200) using a short room code; WebRTC data channel, no backend.
- Added two species to complete rarity tiers: `lunari` (mythical, Spark) and `solaris` (divine, Ember); `elderwood` is legendary boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored `three` 0.184.0 (`vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/three.core.js`).
- Implemented procedural models for all base creatures plus `lunari` and `solaris`, trainer, world props.
- Implemented island world: terrain, pond/ocean, trees, tall grass, flowers, hut, campfire, shrine, pickups, clouds, butterflies, pollen, stars, moon.
- Implemented day/night system in `world.setTimeOfDay()` (sky palette, water tint, stars, moon, window/lantern glow, fireflies).
- Implemented turn-based battle arena, HUD, moves, catching flow replaced with flute melody visuals/notes, XP, leveling, switching, running.
- Implemented data changes: rarity definitions, flutes, catch chance calculation, new species/moves, shiny odds and unique shiny seed generation.
- Implemented shiny appearance module (`src/appearance.js`) and integrated into `buildCreature`/`animateCreature`.
- Created full HTML overlay structure and Android-first CSS (touch joystick, action buttons, safe areas, responsive battle/journal/title).
- Vendor check for PeerJS completed; archive extracted only in `/tmp`, not yet copied to project.

### Active
- Removing obsolete orb-catch code from `battle.js` (old `attemptCatch` and `catchChance` methods still present around lines ~919–1000; references to `inventory.orbs` and `this.orb`).
- Integrating flute inventory/HUD/trade/shiny odds into `src/main.js`.
- Implementing online trade manager/UI with PeerJS.
- Finishing PWA (manifest, icons, service worker) and fullscreen/Android behavior.
- Game not yet started/tested in browser; no screenshots produced.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Remove dead orb capture code from `src/battle.js` and ensure all flute import/use paths are consistent.
2. Update `src/main.js`: replace `inventory.orbs` with `inventory.flutes`, `selectedFlute`, `resonance`; add flute HUD name/count, flute unlock toasts, time-of-day clock progression/save, `world.setTimeOfDay` calls and light updates.
3. Add shiny rendering paths: pass mon objects to `buildCreature`, dynamic shiny thumbnails, shiny badges/unique signature, rarity odds in journal/bestiary, shiny wild prompts.
4. Add special spawns: `lunari` at night (requires aurora), `solaris` by day after boss, legendary `elderwood` post-game; spawn/despawn with day/night.
5. Implement `src/trade.js` trade manager + trade modal UI and add trade button/HUD entry; sanitize received creatures.
6. Copy `peerjs.min.js` from `/tmp/peerjs-1.5.5.tgz` to `vendor/`, include UMD script in `index.html`.
7. Add `manifest.json`, icons, service worker, fullscreen button handler, PWA registration, Android performance defaults.
8. Run via start script, test desktop + mobile viewport with Playwright, fix runtime errors, capture screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: main game loop, state, HUD, world interactions, save/load, quests; needs major integration updates.
- `src/battle.js`: battle logic now using flute capture; contains obsolete orb methods to remove.
- `src/data.js`: species, rarities, flutes, catch chances, shiny odds, creature creation.
- `src/models.js`: procedural models; imports `applyShiny`/`animateShiny`; accepts mon object in `buildCreature`.
- `src/appearance.js`: unique shiny palettes/aura/constellation generation.
- `src/world.js`: world, day/night, sky, pickups, special spawn points.
- `index.html`: HUD, title, starter, battle, modal, ending; needs trade modal + PeerJS script + PWA links.
- `css/style.css`: responsive Android-first UI; needs flute/rarity/shiny/trade styles.
- `src/input.js`: keyboard, pointer orbit, joystick.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural music/SFX; needs `flute(tier)` method.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: vendored renderer library.
- `manifest.json` (missing): PWA manifest.
- `sw.js` (missing): service worker cache.
- `vendor/peerjs.min.js` (missing): copy from `/tmp/peerjs-1.5.5.tgz`.

## Important Context
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; static server supports only `index.html` or Vite; no package.json currently.
- `start.sh` serves via `RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs`; default PORT 3000 (README references 3002).
- `battle.js` currently calls `catchChance(...)` imported from `data.js` in new flute UI, while an old class method of the same name still exists.
- Player inventory object is shared by reference with `Battle`; changing shape to `{flutes, potions, resonance}` requires all `orbs` references removed.
- `createCreature()` now assigns `shiny`, `shinySeed`, and `appearance` based on rarity odds.
- Shiny appearance is derived from `appearance.seed`; `buildCreature(mon)` supports passing the whole creature.
- Existing saves use key `lumen-isles-save-v1`; migration may be needed for flutes/time.
- Audio must initialize from a user gesture for Android; this is already wired.
- Test environment has `playwright-cli`, Chromium, Xvfb/SwiftShader; no GPU acceleration claims.
- User speaks Spanish; respond in Spanish.
- Day/night world method already implemented but not yet called from `main.js`.
- `src/data.js` defines `SHINY_ODDS`, `shinyOdds()`, `FLUTES`, `FLUTE_ORDER`, `RARITIES`, `requiredFluteTier()`, `requiredFlute()`, `catchChance()`.
- New shiny species models are complete but not yet spawnable from world logic.
- Trade system is still entirely unimplemented.

We should answer in Spanish, with concrete options for this project: static server locally, deployment, and a backend for real payments/trading.

Given the ongoing task, I should explain how to create a server:
1. Local static server: `python3 -m http.server 3000` or existing start.sh; no build.
2. Deploy static to GitHub Pages/Netlify/Vercel/Cloudflare Pages; Android installable PWA.
3. For the shop with payments, need a small backend (Node/Express or serverless function) to create Stripe Checkout sessions, receive webhooks, and issue redeem codes. PeerJS cloud for trade means no server required, or self-host PeerServer.
4. Example minimal Node/Express server that serves static files + Stripe checkout + webhook + code generation. Could create files in repo now? The user asks "how can I create a server?" Maybe implement it: add `server/` with package.json, Express static, Stripe checkout, webhook, SQLite or JSON store, redeem endpoint. But the project is static no build; adding optional server is reasonable.

Need decide: Answer with steps and offer to implement. Since they ask "how", a concise guide + offer. But as coding agent, maybe we should actually create the server since the current goal is a shop with payments to their account; a backend solves the limitation. The previous response said can't do payment without server. Now they ask how to create one. This is an invitation to implement a server. Let's implement a minimal production-ish Node server:

- `server/package.json` with express, stripe, dotenv (maybe no DB; use JSON file for orders/codes).
- `server/index.js`:
  - serve `..` static (the game).
  - `POST /api/checkout` {packId} → create Stripe Checkout Session with price_data (amount from server-side pack catalog), metadata {packId, orderId}; success_url `/success.html?session_id=...`; cancel_url.
  - `POST /api/webhook` raw body verify signature; on checkout.session.completed generate code, store in `server/data/codes.json`, optionally email? no email service; display code on success page by polling `/api/order/:sessionId` (but requires session id; safe-ish with session retrieval). Better success page calls `/api/order?session_id=...` and server verifies Stripe session payment_status, then returns code. This avoids email.
  - `GET /api/config` returns public key and enabled.
  - `POST /api/redeem`? Redemption remains client-side; but codes in client JS are insecure. Better server returns signed codes? Since game is client-side and save is local, a code check can be done server-side via `/api/verify-code` with rate limiting, then client stores unlock. Still tamperable. For honest use, okay. But codes currently in shop.js. We can move codes server-side and have client verify? But offline static mode then no codes. Could keep fallback.

- The Stripe webhook requires raw body. Express static.
- Security: validate pack ID against server catalog (not client price), use metadata. Idempotency via `orderId`.
- Codes stored as `{code, packId, sessionId, used:false, createdAt}`. On order retrieval, if paid and code generated, return code. On redeem, client checks local.
- No database; JSON file is fine for small scale. Note single instance.
- Provide `.env.example` with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, PORT, BASE_URL.
- Client integration: shop.js currently uses static link and codes. We can update shop.js to optionally use server API:
  - `PAYMENT.apiBase` default '' (same origin) or config.
  - `payForPack` in main: if `PAYMENT.checkoutEndpoint` and `PAYMENT.apiEnabled`, POST to `/api/checkout` and redirect to `session.url`; else external link.

import math, struct, zlib, os

SS = 3  # supersampling

def rounded_mask(x, y, size, radius):
    r = radius
    if x < r and y < r:
        return (x - r) ** 2 + (y - r) ** 2 <= r * r
    if x > size - r and y < r:
        return (x - (size - r)) ** 2 + (y - r) ** 2 <= r * r
    if x < r and y > size - r:
        return (x - r) ** 2 + (y - (size - r)) ** 2 <= r * r
    if x > size - r and y > size - r:
        return (x - (size - r)) ** 2 + (y - (size - r)) ** 2 <= r * r
    return True

def star_polygon(cx, cy, outer, inner, points=5, rot=-math.pi / 2):
    pts = []
    for i in range(points * 2):
        r = outer if i % 2 == 0 else inner
        a = rot + i * math.pi / points
        pts.append((cx + math.cos(a) * r, cy + math.sin(a) * r))
    return pts

def point_in_poly(x, y, poly):
    inside = False
    j = len(poly) - 1
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        xi, yi = poly[i]
        xj, yj = poly[j]
        if ((yi > y) != (yj > y)) and (x < (xj - xi) * (y - yi) / (yj - yi + 1e-12) + xi):
            inside = not inside
        j = i
    return inside

def make(size, path):
    star = star_polygon(size * 0.5, size * 0.48, size * 0.285, size * 0.115)
    small = star_polygon(size * 0.5, size * 0.48, size * 0.40, size * 0.045, 5, -math.pi / 2)
    rows = []
    for py in range(size):
        row = bytearray()
        for px in range(size):
            r = g = b = a = 0
            for sy in range(SS):
                for sx in range(SS):
                    x = px + (sx + 0.5) / SS
                    y = py + (sy + 0.5) / SS
                    if not rounded_mask(x, y, size, size * 0.22):
                        continue
                    nx = x / size
                    ny = y / size
                    # deep teal gradient
                    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, ny * 0.9 + nx * 0.1))
                    rr = int(18 + 10 * (1 - t))
                    gg = int(52 + 34 * (1 - t))
                    bb = int(52 + 30 * (1 - t))
                    # central glow
                    d = math.hypot(nx - 0.5, ny - 0.46)
                    glow = max(0.0, 1.0 - d / 0.55) ** 2
                    rr = min(255, int(rr + 60 * glow))
                    gg = min(255, int(gg + 78 * glow))
                    bb = min(255, int(bb + 54 * glow))
                    # rings
                    ring = abs(d - 0.34)
                    if ring < 0.008:
                        rr, gg, bb = 242, 211, 130
                    # stars
                    if point_in_poly(x, y, star):
                        rr, gg, bb = 255, 232, 154
                    elif point_in_poly(x, y, small):
                        rr, gg, bb = 120, 224, 214
                    r += rr; g += gg; b += bb; a += 255
            n = SS * SS
            row += bytes((r // n, g // n, b // n, a // n))
        rows.append(bytes(row))
    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + row for row in rows)

    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + tag + data
        return c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xffffffff)

    png = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    png += chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', size, size, 8, 6, 0, 0, 0))
    png += chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw, 9))
    png += chunk(b'IEND', b'')
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(png)
    print(path, size, os.path.getsize(path))

let current = 'es';

export function getLang() {
  return current;
}

export function languageInfo(id = current) {
  return LANGUAGES.find((l) => l.id === id) || LANGUAGES[0];
}

export function t(key, vars = {}, fallback = '') {
  const table = DICT[current] || DICT.en;
  let value = table[key] ?? DICT.en[key] ?? fallback ?? key;
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return value;
  return value.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (m, name) => (vars[name] !== undefined ? String(vars[name]) : m));
}

export function applyI18n(root = document) {
  document.documentElement.lang = current;
  document.title = t('meta.title');
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n]').forEach((el) => {
    el.textContent = t(el.dataset.i18n);
  });
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n-html]').forEach((el) => {
    el.innerHTML = t(el.dataset.i18nHtml);
  });
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n-title]').forEach((el) => {
    el.title = t(el.dataset.i18nTitle);
  });
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n-aria]').forEach((el) => {
    el.setAttribute('aria-label', t(el.dataset.i18nAria));
  });
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n-placeholder]').forEach((el) => {
    el.placeholder = t(el.dataset.i18nPlaceholder);
  });
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-lang]').forEach((btn) => {
    const active = btn.dataset.lang === current;
    btn.classList.toggle('active', active);
    btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(active));
  });
}

export function setLang(id) {
  if (!DICT[id]) return;
  current = id;
  try { localStorage.setItem('lumen-lang', id); } catch { /* storage may be blocked */ }
  applyI18n();
  document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('lumen-lang', { detail: id }));
}

export function initI18n() {
  let saved = null;
  try { saved = localStorage.getItem('lumen-lang'); } catch { /* ignore */ }
  const browser = (navigator.language || 'en').slice(0, 2);
  const pick = DICT[saved] ? saved : DICT[browser] ? browser : 'es';
  current = pick;

  document.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
    const btn = event.target.closest('[data-lang]');
    if (!btn) return;
    setLang(btn.dataset.lang);
  });

  applyI18n();
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build “Lumen Isles”, a 3D monster-collection browser game for Android with day/night, flute-based capture, rarity tiers, unique shinies, online trading, a shop, and multi-language support.
- The game title must be “Colección de Monstruos Mundial” / “World Monster Collection”, with several languages selectable at the start.

## Requirements
- 3D Pokémon-style game, playable on Android phones/tablets with touch controls.
- Dynamic day/night cycle.
- Capture via flutes matched to creature level and rarity.
- Rarities: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, mythical, divine.
- Online creature trading system.
- Every shiny must look unique; shiny odds vary by rarity.
- Shop with unique game items; real-money payments must go to the owner’s account.
- Game title: “Colección de Monstruos Mundial” (localized variants).
- Multiple selectable languages at the beginning of the game.
- Original creatures/art/music; no Pokémon assets or trademarks.
- User speaks Spanish; respond in Spanish.

## Decisions
- Pure static Three.js game, no build step; Three.js vendored locally.
- Flutes: willow (tier 1), silver (2), amber (3), moonstone (4), aurora (5), celestial (6); reusable.
- Required flute tier = rarity tier, +1 for non-legendary rarity at level ≥10; capped at 6.
- Flute unlocks: willow start, silver at 2 species caught, amber at 3, moonstone at 5, aurora at 6, celestial after guardian defeat.
- Shiny odds: common 1/150, uncommon 1/240, rare 1/420, epic 1/750, legendary 1/1600, mythical 1/3000, divine 1/5000.
- Shiny uniqueness via per-creature seed → palette, aura orbiters, star freckles, optional ring, sparkle rhythm.
- Trading uses PeerJS public cloud (`0.peerjs.com`) via six-character room code; WebRTC data channel, no backend.
- Added species `lunari` (mythical, Spark, night, Aurora Flute) and `solaris` (divine, Ember, post-boss day, Celestial Flute); `elderwood` is legendary boss.
- Shop has Lumen currency for supplies/one-of-one curios, plus supporter packs using an external checkout link; real payment requires owner’s Stripe/PayPal/Mercado Pago link.
- Redemption codes are defined in `src/shop.js` (`REDEEM_CODES`); automatic secure delivery would need a backend.
- i18n languages chosen: Spanish (default), English, Portuguese, French.
- New brand title is split into 3 logo lines via `brand.line1/2/3`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored Three.js 0.184.0 and PeerJS 1.5.5 (`vendor/peerjs.min.js`).
- Procedural models, island world, day/night system, battle arena, HUD, touch controls, procedural audio.
- Flute capture system integrated in battle; obsolete orb-catch code removed from `src/battle.js`.
- Rarity definitions, flute requirements, catch chances, shiny odds and unique shiny seed generation in `src/data.js`.
- Unique shiny appearance module `src/appearance.js`, integrated into models, battle, wild spawns, journal and dynamic thumbnails.
- Added `lunari`/`solaris` models and special night/day spawn logic in `main.js`.
- Implemented online trade manager `src/trade.js` with room codes, offers, acceptance, sanitization, unique shiny seed checking, party/ranch exchange; wired to modal UI.
- Implemented shop data and helpers in `src/shop.js` (supplies, one-of-one curios, supporter packs, Lumen, serials, redeem codes, payment link config).
- Added shop UI, buy/pay/redeem handlers, Lumen HUD, flute HUD, time chip, fullscreen handler, trainer cosmetics, shiny wild prompts, ranch creature storage.
- Added PWA manifest, service worker, SVG/PNG icons, PeerJS script tag, service-worker registration.
- Added `src/i18n.js` with es/en/pt/fr dictionaries, `t()`, `applyI18n()`, `setLang()`, `initI18n()`, language persistence.
- Updated `index.html` title, logo lines, language picker, starter/HUD/ending/loading text and i18n attributes.
- Added large CSS block for flutes, rarity chips, shiny UI, journal, shop, trade, language picker styling (language-picker CSS still missing).

### Active
- Finish i18n integration in `src/main.js`, `src/battle.js`, `src/shop.js`, `src/trade.js`: import/call `initI18n`, replace hard-coded strings with `t()`, re-render on `lumen-lang` event.
- Add `.language-picker` / `.lang-btn` CSS and responsive logo sizing for the 3-line title.
- Verify game runs; no browser test or screenshots yet.
- Add optional backend server for Stripe checkout/webhook/redeem if requested.
- Answer user’s question “Como puedo crear un servidor?” with local/static/deploy/payment-backend options.

### Blocked
- Real-money automatic payment delivery cannot be secure without a backend and owner’s payment account credentials/link.

## Next Move
1. Import and call `initI18n()` in `main.js`; apply localized strings to title button metadata, quest text, prompts, journal, shop, trade, battle actions and toasts.
2. Wire `lumen-lang` listener to re-render HUD, quest, journal/shop/trade modal, starter cards and battle UI.
3. Update `showHelp`, `renderPartyModal`, `renderShop`, `openTrade` templates to use `t()`.
4. Use `t()` in `battle.js` for FIGHT/FLUTES/SWAP/RUN, bag hints, boss hint, tonic labels and key logs.
5. Add language picker CSS, 3-line logo sizing, ensure title fits mobile.
6. Run static server, test with Playwright/Chromium, fix runtime errors and capture screenshots.
7. Explain server setup and offer optional Stripe/Express backend files.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: game loop, state, HUD, day/night, shop/trade orchestration, save/load; i18n integration in progress.
- `src/i18n.js`: translations and language selection API.
- `src/shop.js`: shop catalog, payment config, purchases, redeem codes, inventory defaults.
- `src/trade.js`: PeerJS trade manager and trade UI.
- `src/battle.js`: flute battle system; strings still English.
- `src/data.js`: species, rarities, flutes, catch odds, shiny seeds/odds, `makeShinySeed()`.
- `src/appearance.js`: unique shiny palette/aura/signature generation.
- `src/models.js`: procedural creatures, trainer, `buildCreature(mon)`.
- `src/world.js`: terrain, pickups, day/night `setTimeOfDay`, wild spawns.
- `index.html`: title, language picker, HUD, battle, modal, ending, scripts.
- `css/style.css`: full UI; needs language-picker/logo CSS.
- `manifest.json`, `sw.js`, `icons/`: PWA assets.
- `vendor/peerjs.min.js`: trade library.
- `README.md`, `start.sh`: run/deployment context.

## Important Context
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; all files are untracked (`git status` shows `??` for project files).
- No `package.json`; static server supports `index.html` via `start.sh` / runtime default start script; README references OMGithub preview.
- `src/main.js` imports `initI18n`/`t` are not yet added; i18n module exists but is unused.
- `renderPartyModal` and other templates still hard-code English strings.
- `openShop`/`openTrade` set `state.mode='menu'`, disable input, and show `#modal`.
- `closeModal()` calls `trade.leave()` and `trade.destroy()`.
- `state.inventory` shape: `{ flutes, potions, resonance, lumen, owned, skins, lureUntil, badges }`.
- `state.ranchMons` stores creatures when party is full; `state.ranch` mirrors count.
- Save key remains `lumen-isles-save-v1`; migration converts old Star Orbs to Lumen.
- `PAYMENT.link` in `src/shop.js` is empty; supporter checkout buttons show setup instructions until filled.
- Default i18n language is Spanish; saved choice uses localStorage key `lumen-lang`.
- Language picker buttons use `data-lang="es|en|pt|fr"`; click handler is registered inside `initI18n()`.
- PeerJS trade requires `vendor/peerjs.min.js` loaded before the module; script tag added.
- Test environment uses Playwright/SwiftShader; no GPU acceleration claims.
- Service worker caches core assets under `lumen-isles-v3`.

messages.text: Puedes hacer las criaturas y los personajes en 2d y dejar el mundo en 3d? Y el diseño de las criaturas debe ser epico

content.text:
The user now wants the creatures and characters in 2D while keeping the world 3D, with epic creature designs. This is a significant pivot from procedural 3D models. Need to respond in Spanish and implement.

We need to decide approach: billboarded 2D sprites (hand-drawn/procedural SVG/canvas art) in the 3D world. The current models.js builds creatures from 3D primitives. We could create epic 2D creature sprites via procedural SVG/canvas, rendered as Sprite or plane billboards, with animations via frame swaps / squash, and a 2D trainer sprite. This is feasible.

Need to inspect models.js architecture and how creatures are built/used. The checkpoint says models.js procedural creatures, buildCreature(mon), buildTrainer, animateCreature, animateTrainer, shadowBlob, material. We need to modify to return 2D sprite groups. However battle uses buildCreature and animateCreature; thumbnails render with buildCreature in a 3D scene. If buildCreature becomes a sprite group, thumbnails still work (sprite rendered with renderer). But `buildCreature` used for battle models with rotations etc; sprite always faces camera, so rotation doesn't matter. Animations currently use animateCreature to move parts; we'd need to implement sprite-based animation (bob, squash, tilt, frame changes). Could keep API.

The user says "criaturas y personajes en 2d" (creatures and characters in 2D) while world stays 3D, and creature design should be epic. We should implement high-quality 2D artwork, likely via procedural canvas or inline SVG. Need originality (no Pokémon assets). We can generate detailed SVG illustrations per species, with gradients, outlines, glowing effects, layered shapes. Could create an `art.js` module with SVG strings for 10 species and trainer, plus shiny palette variants. Render to texture for Three.js sprites. Also use high-res assets for thumbnails/battle. Maybe the sprites should stay readable at various distances.

Current `models.js` likely is 722 lines of geometry. We need to rework. Let's inspect it.

We need to convert models to 2D. Let's think about the best implementation that maintains behavior and visual quality.

Approach:
- Create `src/art2d.js` with SVG markup for each species and trainer, generated from a rich procedural vector design "epic" style: silhouettes with thick outlines, gradients, glowing eyes, elemental effects, layered anatomy. Each species should have custom hand-authored SVG groups. We can design 10 species + trainer. That's a lot of SVG but doable with careful reusable primitives.

- Use SVG data URLs to create `THREE.Texture` via `TextureLoader` or `Image`. Since textures load async, buildCreature currently synchronous and returns group immediately. We can use `CanvasTexture` with canvas drawing; drawing synchronously from SVG requires async image load. Alternative generate artwork on `<canvas>` with 2D API synchronously. Canvas drawing can create equally epic art with gradients, shapes, glows, etc., and gives immediate textures. This is better for sync and no async textures. We can create a 1024x1024 canvas per species (cached), draw detailed vector-like art with paths, gradients, shadows. For shiny variants, generate a variant canvas with palette shifts and extra sparkles (per unique seed), preserving uniqueness.

- Use `THREE.Sprite` with `SpriteMaterial({map, transparent:true, alphaTest:0.01, depthWrite:false})` inside a group. Sprites always face camera. Add an invisible ground shadow via existing shadowBlob.

- Scaling: sprites need consistent world height. Current creatures are ~1.2-2.2 units tall. We can set sprite scale based on species (e.g., 2.2 x 2.2 for small, 3.5 for elderwood). The group origin should be at feet. Sprite center is middle; set sprite.position.y = height/2. Use `sprite.scale.set(w, h, 1)`.

- Animation: Sprites can bob, tilt (material.rotation), squash via scale x/y, and switch between two or three frames for walking/idle/blink. Generating multiple frames per species is heavy but feasible via draw functions taking pose parameters. We can draw on demand to a canvas per frame? Use one texture and animate transform (breathe, sway, hop), plus a secondary "aura" sprite behind, and occasional blink by swapping to a cached blink texture. Also "epic" effects: elemental particles orbiting? We can add 3D particle sprites around the 2D character to give depth without making the character 3D. But user asked characters 2D; effects can be 3D. Keep subtle.

- The thumbnails in main.js use a Three.js renderer to render `buildCreature(mon)` on a transparent background. Sprites render fine, but because the thumbnail camera is angled, sprite faces camera and appears correctly. Good. However, `tr.render(s, cam)` with Sprite might be fine. The existing `buildCreature` sets rotation etc. Sprite ignores rotation except material rotation. Good.

- Battle: `makeModel` sets `g.rotation.y = ...`, `g.userData.basePos`, etc. Sprite group still works. `animateCreature` can update material rotation and position. `spawnScale` adjusts group scale. The lunge moves group. Good. Shadows aren't added in battle to sprites, but okay. Need sprite rendering order/depth: using depthTest true by default; sprite is a plane at z position. In battle, enemy and player face camera at different positions, which may cause overlap but fine.

- World: `spawnWild` adds shadow blob separately; good. BuildCreature group with sprite; scale set. At camera angles, sprites always face camera. Epic.

- Trainer: 2D sprite. `buildTrainer` returns group with sprite and shadow? main adds trainer; no separate shadow. Add a shadow blob in group. animateTrainer: bob and tilt/sway, maybe two-frame walk. `player.facing` sets group.rotation.y but sprite always faces camera, so trainer will always face camera. That's acceptable for 2D sprites. Could flip horizontally based on movement direction by setting material.map to mirrored texture or scale.x negative? Sprite scale.x negative might mirror. But if always facing camera, flipping based on movement makes it look directional. We can compute in animateTrainer? It doesn't have movement direction. main calls `trainer.rotation.y = player.facing`; we could set sprite material.rotation? Not. We could use sprite.center? Hmm. We can just always face camera; that's a common 2.5D style (e.g., Don't Starve-ish? Actually 2D sprites in 3D world). Fine.

- We need "epic" design. The canvas art must be genuinely detailed: dramatic poses, elemental auras, layered wings, armor-like features, glowing eyes, dynamic composition. We can design each creature as a stylized "monster card" full-body pose with strong silhouette. Use gradients, rim light, outlines, glow. The previous creatures are cute; user asks epic. We should reinterpret them as epic but still original. Could keep names but make them more majestic.

Design direction:
- Spriglet: a leaf-fox guardian with antler-like branch ears, flowing leafy tail, emerald armor plates, glowing amber eyes, vine aura. Pose: standing on hind legs? Or dynamic side profile. Epic.
- Emberpup: a lava hound with obsidian paws, flame mane and tail, glowing cracks, ember particles.

## Objective
- Build “Lumen Isles”, a 3D monster-collection browser game for Android with day/night, flute-based capture, rarity tiers, unique shinies, online trading, a shop, and multi-language support.
- The game title must be “Colección de Monstruos Mundial” / “World Monster Collection”, with several languages selectable at the start.

## Requirements
- 3D Pokémon-style game, playable on Android phones/tablets with touch controls.
- Dynamic day/night cycle.
- Capture via flutes matched to creature level and rarity.
- Rarities: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, mythical, divine.
- Online creature trading system.
- Every shiny must look unique; shiny odds vary by rarity.
- Shop with unique game items; real-money payments must go to the owner’s account.
- Game title: “Colección de Monstruos Mundial” (localized variants).
- Multiple selectable languages at the beginning of the game.
- Original creatures/art/music; no Pokémon assets or trademarks.
- User speaks Spanish; respond in Spanish.

## Decisions
- Pure static Three.js game, no build step; Three.js vendored locally.
- Flutes: willow (tier 1), silver (2), amber (3), moonstone (4), aurora (5), celestial (6); reusable.
- Required flute tier = rarity tier, +1 for non-legendary rarity at level ≥10; capped at 6.
- Flute unlocks: willow start, silver at 2 species caught, amber at 3, moonstone at 5, aurora at 6, celestial after guardian defeat.
- Shiny odds: common 1/150, uncommon 1/240, rare 1/420, epic 1/750, legendary 1/1600, mythical 1/3000, divine 1/5000.
- Shiny uniqueness via per-creature seed → palette, aura orbiters, star freckles, optional ring, sparkle rhythm.
- Trading uses PeerJS public cloud (`0.peerjs.com`) via six-character room code; WebRTC data channel, no backend.
- Added species `lunari` (mythical, Spark, night, Aurora Flute) and `solaris` (divine, Ember, post-boss day, Celestial Flute); `elderwood` is legendary boss.
- Shop has Lumen currency for supplies/one-of-one curios, plus supporter packs using an external checkout link; real payment requires owner’s Stripe/PayPal/Mercado Pago link.
- Redemption codes are defined in `src/shop.js` (`REDEEM_CODES`); automatic secure delivery would need a backend.
- i18n languages chosen: Spanish (default), English, Portuguese, French.
- New brand title split into 3 logo lines via `brand.line1/2/3`.
- Dynamic in-game content (types, rarities, flute names/descriptions, move names, lore, toasts, prompts, battle/trade/shop messages) added as a second-pass `EXTRA` dictionary merged into `DICT` in `src/i18n.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored Three.js 0.184.0 and PeerJS 1.5.5 (`vendor/peerjs.min.js`).
- Procedural models, island world, day/night system, battle arena, HUD, touch controls, procedural audio.
- Flute capture system integrated in battle; obsolete orb-catch code removed from `src/battle.js`.
- Rarity definitions, flute requirements, catch chances, shiny odds and unique shiny seed generation in `src/data.js`.
- Unique shiny appearance module `src/appearance.js`, integrated into models, battle, wild spawns, journal and dynamic thumbnails.
- Added `lunari`/`solaris` models and special night/day spawn logic in `main.js`.
- Implemented online trade manager `src/trade.js` with room codes, offers, acceptance, sanitization, unique shiny seed checking, party/ranch exchange; wired to modal UI.
- Implemented shop data and helpers in `src/shop.js` (supplies, one-of-one curios, supporter packs, Lumen, serials, redeem codes, payment link config).
- Added shop UI, buy/pay/redeem handlers, Lumen HUD, flute HUD, time chip, fullscreen handler, trainer cosmetics, shiny wild prompts, ranch creature storage.
- Added PWA manifest, service worker, SVG/PNG icons, PeerJS script tag, service-worker registration.
- Added `src/i18n.js` with es/en/pt/fr dictionaries, `t()`, `applyI18n()`, `setLang()`, `initI18n()`, language persistence.
- Updated `index.html` title/logo lines, language picker, starter/HUD/ending/loading text and i18n attributes.
- Added large CSS block for flutes, rarity chips, shiny UI, journal, shop, trade, language picker styling still missing.
- Created second-pass `EXTRA` i18n dictionary covering types, rarities, flutes, moves, species lore, toasts, prompts, shop/trade/battle dynamic messages, and added merge loop into `DICT`.

### Active
- Finish i18n integration in `src/main.js`, `src/battle.js`, `src/shop.js`, `src/trade.js`: import/call `initI18n`, replace hard-coded strings with `t()` and helper functions, re-render on `lumen-lang` event.
- Add helper functions (`typeName`, `rarityName`, `fluteName`, `moveName`, `speciesLore`) to `src/i18n.js` and update `applyI18n()` to set localized meta description.
- Add `.language-picker` / `.lang-btn` CSS and responsive 3-line logo sizing for mobile.
- Verify game runs; no browser test or screenshots yet.
- Add optional backend server for Stripe checkout/webhook/redeem if requested.
- Answer user’s question “Como puedo crear un servidor?” with local/static/deploy/payment-backend options.

### Blocked
- Real-money automatic payment delivery cannot be secure without a backend and owner’s payment account credentials/link.

## Next Move
1. Add i18n helper functions and meta-description handling to `src/i18n.js`.
2. Import and call `initI18n()` in `main.js`; apply localized strings to title button metadata, quest text, prompts, journal, shop, trade, battle actions and toasts.
3. Add a `lumen-lang` listener to re-render HUD, quest, journal/shop/trade modal, starter cards, ending stats and battle UI; track `state.modalView` and make trade remount safe.
4. Update `showHelp`, `renderPartyModal`, `renderShop`, `openTrade` templates to use `t()`; localize shop item/pack display names, blurbs and perks.
5. Use `t()` and data helpers in `battle.js` for FIGHT/FLUTES/SWAP/RUN, bag hints, boss hint, tonic labels, combat logs and level labels; add `battle.refreshLabels()`.
6. Use `t()` in `trade.js` for all lobby/status/error/log strings; make `mount()` handlers idempotent via `root.onclick`/`root.onkeydown`.
7. Use `t()` in `shop.js` purchase/redeem messages.
8. Add language picker CSS, 3-line logo sizing, ensure title fits mobile.
9. Run static server, test with Playwright/Chromium, fix runtime errors and capture screenshots.
10. Explain server setup and offer optional Stripe/Express backend files.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: game loop, state, HUD, day/night, shop/trade orchestration, save/load; i18n integration pending.
- `src/i18n.js`: translations, `EXTRA` dictionary, language selection API; helper functions still to add.
- `src/battle.js`: flute battle system; all combat/UI strings still English.
- `src/trade.js`: PeerJS trade manager and trade UI; all strings still English.
- `src/shop.js`: shop catalog, payment config, purchases, redeem codes, inventory defaults; messages still English.
- `index.html`: title, language picker, HUD, battle, modal, ending, scripts.
- `css/style.css`: full UI; needs language-picker/logo CSS.
- `src/data.js`: species, rarities, flutes, catch odds, shiny seeds/odds, `makeShinySeed()`.
- `src/appearance.js`: unique shiny palette/aura/signature generation.
- `src/models.js`: procedural creatures, trainer, `buildCreature(mon)`.
- `src/world.js`: terrain, pickups, day/night `setTimeOfDay`, wild spawns.
- `manifest.json`, `sw.js`, `icons/`: PWA assets.
- `vendor/peerjs.min.js`: trade library.
- `README.md`, `start.sh`: run/deployment context.

## Important Context
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; all files are untracked (`git status` shows `??` for project files).
- No `package.json`; static server supports `index.html` via `start.sh` / runtime default start script; README references OMGithub preview.
- `renderPartyModal` and other templates still hard-code English strings.
- `openShop`/`openTrade` set `state.mode='menu'`, disable input, and show `#modal`.
- `closeModal()` calls `trade.leave()` and `trade.destroy()`.
- `state.inventory` shape: `{ flutes, potions, resonance, lumen, owned, skins, lureUntil, badges }`.
- `state.ranchMons` stores creatures when party is full; `state.ranch` mirrors count.
- Save key remains `lumen-isles-save-v1`; migration converts old Star Orbs to Lumen.
- `PAYMENT.link` in `src/shop.js` is empty; supporter checkout buttons show setup instructions until filled.
- Default i18n language is Spanish; saved choice uses localStorage key `lumen-lang`.
- Language picker buttons use `data-lang="es|en|pt|fr"`; click handler is registered inside `initI18n()`.
- PeerJS trade requires `vendor/peerjs.min.js` loaded before the module; script tag added.
- Test environment uses Playwright/SwiftShader; no GPU acceleration claims.
- Service worker caches core assets under `lumen-isles-v3`.
- `buildStarterCards()` currently adds a new click listener on every call; should switch to an idempotent `onclick` to avoid duplicate starter selection.
- `state.zone` currently stores English zone names; refactor to zone IDs and translate via `zone.*` keys.
- `buildStarterCards`, `renderPartyModal`, `renderShop`, `openTrade`, `showEnding` need dynamic re-render on language change; `battle.js` needs a menu-state refresh method.

content.text:
Now add gyms and colosseum. Need design files:

`src/gyms.js`:
- GYMS array with id, name, leader, type, position {x,z}, colors, team species/levels, badge {id,name,glyph,color}, intro/dialogue, requirement maybe badges before.
- 4 gyms:
  1. Bloomfield Gym "Verdant Hall" leader Tilo? But Tilo is NPC botanist. Use unique leaders: "Mara" leaf, at Bloomfield (z 48). Team: mosswarden lv 12, mossling lv 10? Single battle limitation. Could use signature one, but requirement leaders. Maybe support a gym team of 2-3 via sequential battles. Let's extend Battle to support enemyTeam.

Let's examine Battle finish and enemy faint. `enemyFainted()` around 680?

Enemy fainted -> award xp -> finish. To support gym teams, modify:
- `begin(enemy, isBoss, onEnd, opts={})` where opts.team = [mons], opts.trainerName, opts.isGym.
- maintain `this.enemyTeam`, `this.enemyIndex`.
- `enemy` getter? It's set property. At start: `this.enemyTeam = opts.team?.length ? opts.team : [enemy]; this.enemyIndex = 0; this.enemy = this.enemyTeam[0]`. Need enemy at begin param may equal team[0].
- On `enemyFainted`: if more team members: log leader sends next, spawn model for next at -3.1, reset stages, update HUD, busy false renderMain; return. Else award xp finish.
- Kicker/trainer: "GYM LEADER MARA" etc.
- Catch disabled for trainer battles: in renderBag or playFlute, if this.trainerBattle, log can't capture another trainer's partner. Currently isBoss blocks. Add `this.noCatch` for gym/colosseum.
- Enemy attack logs "Wild X used" -> if trainerBattle: `${trainerName}'s X used`.

Level scaling: gym teams created via createCreature, with hp full.

Main integration:
- `startGymBattle(gym)` checks not defeated? Badges in state.inventory.badges. If badge already, allow rematch? award no badge.
- Battle begin(gym.team[0], false, cb, {team:gym.team, trainerName:gym.leader, gymId:gym.id, noCatch:true}).
- endBattle result 'win' and wild.gym? We pass a special object `{mon: team[0], gym}` as wild. In endBattle branch `result==='win'`: if wild.gym and not badge → award badge, lumen, unlock; toast. Need distinguish gym battle from normal trainer.
- Boss remains.

Gym world objects: create in `src/gyms.js` buildGymWorld? We can create simple structures in main using THREE and add colliders. Better `src/gymworld.js` exports `createGyms(scene, world)` returning array of gym objects with positions, meshes, leader sprite (buildPerson profile custom), and `nearby(pos)`.

But leader profiles in art2d are fixed keys. Add gym leader looks to NPC_LOOKS or use generic profiles. We can add 4 new looks: `mara`, `brann`, `sable`, `orin?`. Or reuse `tilo`, `sol`, etc. Better add new distinct entries: `mara` (leaf), `brann` (stone), `sable` (aqua), `kael` (spark/ember). We'll add to NPC_LOOKS.

Gyms locations:
- Verdant Hall (leaf) at Bloomfield (12, 52) leader Mara, party mosswarden lv12, spriglet? Use mossling lv10 + mosswarden lv13.
- Tideglass Grotto (aqua) at pond east (52, 22) leader Sable, dropplet lv13 + tidalyn lv16.
- Cinder Forge (ember) at Cinder Hollow (-20,-40) leader Kael, emberpup lv15 + pyrohound lv18.
- Stormspire Colosseum? Actually gym 4 stone/ spark at West Thicket (-46, -12) leader Brann, pebblit lv15 + cragwarden lv18 + voltrix lv17.
Progression: need badges count to challenge next? Make free order but recommended. Gate colosseum behind 2 badges? User wants coliseum; unlock after first badge.

Gym structures: build a distinctive ring/platform, banners with gym color, torch lights, leader sprite standing. Could be simple but attractive. Use material from models; add `THREE.Group` at location. Add colliders for pillars maybe. Add send prompt when near. Interaction priority: NPCs, gyms, landmarks before camp? We'll integrate.

Badges UI: add a badge row in journal + HUD maybe small icons. inventory.badges currently strings for supporter badges; use `gym-<id>` entries. Add `BADGES` definitions in gyms.js; journal displays.

Colosseum PvP:
- World structure at a central-ish location maybe (0, 40) "Coliseo del Alba" with large arches. Add keeper NPC. Interact opens colosseum modal.
- `src/colosseum.js`: manager using PeerJS. Need to check trade.js connect pattern; copy simplified. P2P handshake:
  - host creates peer id `lumen-colosseum-<code>`, join connects to that.
  - exchange `hello` with player name and team snapshot (party of up to 3, sanitized).
  - both click "Ready"; host receives, when both ready generate seed, compute battle, send `result` with seed and log/winner; guest computes same using seed. Deterministic sim must use own RNG and team order identical. Host sends seed + hostTeam + guestTeam maybe; guest already has both. To guarantee same, host sends full payload {seed, teams:[host,guest], winner, log}. Guest renders log. Host also.
  - Simulation: 1v1 active from each team, turn order by spd, each uses strongest effective move. Damage deterministic using RNG seeded. Continue until all faint. Log rounds. This is an auto-battle; can be labeled "Simulación de combate" and both watch.
  - Better allow "choose your lead" by selecting order in UI (team list reorder? simpler team = party order; user can choose lead via dropdown/buttons). We can let players click a creature to set lead; send team rotated.
  - Rewards: winner +120 Lumen, loser +30, track `state.colosseumWins` maybe save.
  - Need state mutation via callbacks in main.
- `src/colosseum.js` UI in modal, imported in main; on complete callback gives winner and lumen. Could integrate `onFinished(winner)`.

Given time, implement a simple but functional P2P colosseum. Must ensure PeerJS available. Network may not be testable but syntax/UI.

Also add "practice duel" vs AI? Not necessary but useful when no friend. Maybe "Entrenamiento" against a phantom champion using same simulation; user can test. Could add AI opponent button to make feature usable. Good.

Story quest integration should include gyms: main story chapter 3 maybe "The Four Seals" requiring 2 badges before guardian? User asked long story; add main chapters:
- Keep existing 3-phase logic replaced by story.js:
  1. catch 3
  2. 2 gym badges + discover 4 zones
  3. guardian
  4. 4 badges + 3 dawn shards + catch Lunari/Solaris
  5. all 10 species + 4 side quests → final.
